{
  "project_id": "P-SRB-CompetitivenessJobs",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Weak strategic planning and policy coordination may limit the effectiveness of reforms and reduce expected competitiveness gains.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen the inter‑ministerial PPMC Working Group, define clear mandates, schedule semi‑annual reviews, and provide capacity‑building workshops for all ministries.",
      "evidence": "Weak strategic planning and policy coordination are identified as main challenges; policy coordination is among the weakest points for Serbia (Section A.1, B.11)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Implementing agencies (PPS, MoE, MoESTD, MoLEVSA) have limited experience with World Bank fiduciary and procurement procedures, risking implementation delays.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit experienced consultants, deliver targeted training on Bank procurement and financial management, and establish standard operating procedures with regular performance monitoring.",
      "evidence": "Most entities involved have no experience in implementing World Bank‑funded projects and with Bank procurement (IV.D.86‑87)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Insufficient procurement capacity in PPS may cause procurement delays and non‑compliance with Bank guidelines.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Hire a dedicated procurement specialist, conduct intensive procurement training for PPS staff, and use Bank technical assistance for bid preparation and contract management.",
      "evidence": "Assessment concluded PPS lacks adequate capacity in Bank‑funded projects and procurement; procurement expert to be hired (IV.D.86‑88)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Failure to achieve Disbursement‑Linked Indicators (DLIs) could trigger waivers or withheld loan disbursements, affecting cash flow.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Set up a real‑time DLI tracking system, verify evidence early, and prepare contingency action plans for any missed indicator to request timely reassessment.",
      "evidence": "DLIs condition disbursements; failure to achieve triggers waivers or withheld payments (III.A.22‑23, IV.A.58)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Annual budget allocations for matching grants and the Technology Transfer Facility may not be approved, limiting innovation financing.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Secure legislative commitment for the required budget lines, embed allocations in multi‑year budget cycles, and monitor approvals through quarterly fiscal reviews.",
      "evidence": "DLI 3 and DLI 4 require annual budget allocations (EUR 0.9 mn for TTF, EUR 2.7 mn for matching grants) (DLI 3, DLI 4)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "High caseload per NES case worker (200‑2,000) reduces quality of employer services and job matching.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Redesign caseload distribution, introduce an active‑job‑seeker registry, re‑allocate staff across branches, and hire temporary case workers where needed.",
      "evidence": "Average caseload varies between around 200 to over 2,000 registered unemployed per case worker (Component 4, 46)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Low certification rate of NES case workers may hinder professional service delivery and DLI 6 compliance.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop and mandate a certification curriculum, set a target of 85 % certified case workers, and conduct quarterly compliance audits.",
      "evidence": "DLI 6 requires 85 % of NES case workers certified; current certification 0 % (DLI 6 description)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "High tax wedge and benefit withdrawal for low‑wage earners create strong disincentives to formal employment, limiting job creation.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Design and pilot an in‑work cash‑transfer scheme, adjust tax and social‑security contributions for part‑time jobs, and enact supporting legislation.",
      "evidence": "Serbia has one of the highest tax wedges on low‑paying jobs; benefits reduced for each dinar earned (Section 52‑53)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Overlapping mandates among investment and export promotion agencies risk inefficiency and misallocation of public resources.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Conduct a comprehensive agency audit, develop a consolidation roadmap, clarify legal mandates, and implement governance reforms with performance targets.",
      "evidence": "Investment promotion agencies have overlapping mandates, no coordination, and unclear links to policy goals (Section 4.11‑12)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Elevated public debt (>70 % of GDP) and ongoing fiscal consolidation could constrain fiscal space for project‑related expenditures.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Align project spending with the IMF Stand‑By Agreement, maintain strict budget discipline, and build a contingency reserve for fiscal shocks.",
      "evidence": "Public debt to GDP rose from 36 % in 2009 to over 70 % in 2014; fiscal consolidation ongoing (Section 1.A.1‑2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Data quality and integration issues in NES and ALMP monitoring may impair evidence‑based policy adjustments.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Upgrade the NES Management Information System, standardize data collection protocols, provide staff IT training, and institute regular data‑quality audits.",
      "evidence": "NES data collection is extensive but needs better translation into analysis; risk of insufficient data for ALMP redesign (Section 4.B)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Innovation grants (Mini & Matching) could generate indirect environmental impacts not covered by the Category B classification.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Apply the Environmental and Social Management Framework to all grant‑related activities, require environmental screening, and monitor compliance with mitigation measures.",
      "evidence": "Possible indirect environmental impacts may arise under Component 2 on Innovation, especially Mini & Matching Grant programs (Section F.90‑91)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Future political changes or loss of coalition support could weaken commitment to reform implementation.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Secure cross‑party endorsement of the reform agenda, embed key actions in legislation, and maintain continuous stakeholder dialogue to preserve political buy‑in.",
      "evidence": "Two successive elections in 2012 and 2014 created a new coalition; future shifts could affect reform agenda (Section 1.A.2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Serbia’s low ranking in business environment (e.g., construction permits, tax payments) may deter private investment needed for job creation.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement best‑practice investment promotion reforms, streamline permit processes, introduce one‑stop services, and monitor improvements via World Bank Doing Business indicators.",
      "evidence": "Serbia ranks 91st out of 189 in Doing Business; construction permits and tax payment are the worst indicators (Section 9)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "High perceived corruption could lead to procurement delays and reduced donor confidence.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Enforce public disclosure of all contracts, strengthen anti‑corruption controls, conduct independent audits, and publish procurement progress on agency websites.",
      "evidence": "Perceived level of corruption in the country is high; procurement risk rated high (IV.D.86‑87, risk table)."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Weak strategic planning and policy coordination may limit the effectiveness of reforms and reduce expected competitiveness gains.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen the inter‑ministerial PPMC Working Group, define clear mandates, schedule semi‑annual reviews, and provide capacity‑building workshops for all ministries.
risks.evidence: Weak strategic planning and policy coordination are identified as main challenges; policy coordination is among the weakest points for Serbia (Section A.1, B.11).

risks.description: Implementing agencies (PPS, MoE, MoESTD, MoLEVSA) have limited experience with World Bank fiduciary and procurement procedures, risking implementation delays.
risks.mitigation: Recruit experienced consultants, deliver targeted training on Bank procurement and financial management, and establish standard operating procedures with regular performance monitoring.
risks.evidence: Most entities involved have no experience in implementing World Bank‑funded projects and with Bank procurement (IV.D.86‑87).

risks.description: Insufficient procurement capacity in PPS may cause procurement delays and non‑compliance with Bank guidelines.
risks.mitigation: Hire a dedicated procurement specialist, conduct intensive procurement training for PPS staff, and use Bank technical assistance for bid preparation and contract management.
risks.evidence: Assessment concluded PPS lacks adequate capacity in Bank‑funded projects and procurement; procurement expert to be hired (IV.D.86‑88).

risks.description: Failure to achieve Disbursement‑Linked Indicators (DLIs) could trigger waivers or withheld loan disbursements, affecting cash flow.
risks.mitigation: Set up a real‑time DLI tracking system, verify evidence early, and prepare contingency action plans for any missed indicator to request timely reassessment.
risks.evidence: DLIs condition disbursements; failure to achieve triggers waivers or withheld payments (III.A.22‑23, IV.A.58).

risks.description: Annual budget allocations for matching grants and the Technology Transfer Facility may not be approved, limiting innovation financing.
risks.mitigation: Secure legislative commitment for the required budget lines, embed allocations in multi‑year budget cycles, and monitor approvals through quarterly fiscal reviews.
risks.evidence: DLI 3 and DLI 4 require annual budget allocations (EUR 0.9 mn for TTF, EUR 2.7 mn for matching grants) (DLI 3, DLI 4).

risks.description: High caseload per NES case worker (200‑2,000) reduces quality of employer services and job matching.
risks.mitigation: Redesign caseload distribution, introduce an active‑job‑seeker registry, re‑allocate staff across branches, and hire temporary case workers where needed.
risks.evidence: Average caseload varies between around 200 to over 2,000 registered unemployed per case worker (Component 4, 46).

risks.description: Low certification rate of NES case workers may hinder professional service delivery and DLI 6 compliance.
risks.mitigation: Develop and mandate a certification curriculum, set a target of 85 % certified case workers, and conduct quarterly compliance audits.
risks.evidence: DLI 6 requires 85 % of NES case workers certified; current certification 0 % (DLI 6 description).

risks.description: High tax wedge and benefit withdrawal for low‑wage earners create strong disincentives to formal employment, limiting job creation.
risks.mitigation: Design and pilot an in‑work cash‑transfer scheme, adjust tax and social‑security contributions for part‑time jobs, and enact supporting legislation.
risks.evidence: Serbia has one of the highest tax wedges on low‑paying jobs; benefits reduced for each dinar earned (Section 52‑53).

risks.description: Overlapping mandates among investment and export promotion agencies risk inefficiency and misallocation of public resources.
risks.mitigation: Conduct a comprehensive agency audit, develop a consolidation roadmap, clarify legal mandates, and implement governance reforms with performance targets.
risks.evidence: Investment promotion agencies have overlapping mandates, no coordination, and unclear links to policy goals (Section 4.11‑12).

risks.description: Elevated public debt (>70 % of GDP) and ongoing fiscal consolidation could constrain fiscal space for project‑related expenditures.
risks.mitigation: Align project spending with the IMF Stand‑By Agreement, maintain strict budget discipline, and build a contingency reserve for fiscal shocks.
risks.evidence: Public debt to GDP rose from 36 % in 2009 to over 70 % in 2014; fiscal consolidation ongoing (Section 1.A.1‑2).

risks.description: Data quality and integration issues in NES and ALMP monitoring may impair evidence‑based policy adjustments.
risks.mitigation: Upgrade the NES Management Information System, standardize data collection protocols, provide staff IT training, and institute regular data‑quality audits.
risks.evidence: NES data collection is extensive but needs better translation into analysis; risk of insufficient data for ALMP redesign (Section 4.B).

risks.description: Innovation grants (Mini & Matching) could generate indirect environmental impacts not covered by the Category B classification.
risks.mitigation: Apply the Environmental and Social Management Framework to all grant‑related activities, require environmental screening, and monitor compliance with mitigation measures.
risks.evidence: Possible indirect environmental impacts may arise under Component 2 on Innovation, especially Mini & Matching Grant programs (Section F.90‑91).

risks.description: Future political changes or loss of coalition support could weaken commitment to reform implementation.
risks.mitigation: Secure cross‑party endorsement of the reform agenda, embed key actions in legislation, and maintain continuous stakeholder dialogue to preserve political buy‑in.
risks.evidence: Two successive elections in 2012 and 2014 created a new coalition; future shifts could affect reform agenda (Section 1.A.2).

risks.description: Serbia’s low ranking in business environment (e.g., construction permits, tax payments) may deter private investment needed for job creation.
risks.mitigation: Implement best‑practice investment promotion reforms, streamline permit processes, introduce one‑stop services, and monitor improvements via World Bank Doing Business indicators.
risks.evidence: Serbia ranks 91st out of 189 in Doing Business; construction permits and tax payment are the worst indicators (Section 9).

risks.description: High perceived corruption could lead to procurement delays and reduced donor confidence.
risks.mitigation: Enforce public disclosure of all contracts, strengthen anti‑corruption controls, conduct independent audits, and publish procurement progress on agency websites.
risks.evidence: Perceived level of corruption in the country is high; procurement risk rated high (IV.D.86‑87, risk table).
